scope: Use safe fixed-size rows for eight-lane arithmetic, preserving aliased operands by copying input rows. Expand full active blocks for cheap arithmetic; keep compact loops for division, remainder and larger math bodies. Separate register resizing from the VM constructor. No bytecode, wire, heap-storage or frame-cache change. Pointwise program fusion remains unfinished.
method: ESP32 rev3.1, 240 MHz, one core, Wi-Fi off, GPIO untouched. Cargo release opt-level 3, fat LTO, one codegen unit. Compare the uniform-sampling image with the final lane-arithmetic image using byte-identical archives, timestamps and expected outputs. Each timing window includes 32 frames and first use. Two-second controls bracket 997/1999 us PC sampling. Instruction instrumentation is absent. This is a native-code change across images, not a same-image A/B claim. Excludes network, storage, DMA and physical output; no laptop timing comparison.

correctness.focused_tests: 126 runtime unit tests pass. Added coverage checks every lane mask and every source/destination alias combination for arithmetic. Existing tests cover numeric divergence, temporal loops, seeks, tails, resource sampling and automation.

validation: cargo fmt and 126 runtime unit tests pass. Complete controller release image builds. Ten measured product-source files matched the checkout before the subsequent compiler changes. Full pnpm check passed, including device-storage tests and workspace Clippy.

implementation_comparison.tradeoff: Expanding every operation improved timing but exceeded the complete controller's instruction-memory region by 5800 bytes. A dynamic-count loop was slower and larger. Expanding only cheap operations plus separating register resizing recovers most of the gain and fits the complete controller. The final image is 809 us slower than the selective-only prototype; call/placement costs are not isolated. Resizing accounts for about 0.8% of final mixed self-symbol samples. No opcode handler moved out of the interpreter.

cold_cost: Several cheap workloads have roughly 120 us higher first-use cost after outlining register resizing: black first frame 282 to 402 us and starter 483 to 602 us. Black mean changes 128 to 131 us and starter 224 to 227 us, while their p95 stays essentially unchanged. Representative mixed, Shimmer, Chase and Stanford playback improve; no complexity was added to recover tiny isolated means.

controller.note: The interpreter and lane-control helpers remain in instruction memory. Resizing is an ordinary out-of-line initialization routine. Stack figures are individual reservations, not a maximum recursive stack bound. Playback retained allocations are unchanged for all 25 measured cases.

hotspot_percent.note: Weighted self-symbol shares from both sampling periods; estimates do not isolate opcode costs or effect/operator callers.

limits: Mixed is 7.3% faster than the previous image and 2.66x faster than the 291705 us staged/block baseline, still far above the 16.667 ms budget. Shimmer 1200, Chase/Pulse 16 layers and Stanford fit all 32 measured evaluation deadlines. These windows do not establish full-show worst cases or physical-output performance.

Sibling lane-rows, lane-rows-full, lane-rows-counted and lane-rows-selective directories retain the measured diagnostic variants. Only this reviewed summary is retained outside target.
